name: AD — Service/Privileged Account Logon from Novel Source
description: A privileged or service account authenticated over the network (logon type 3) or via RDP (type 10) from a source IP it has never used in the last 30 days. Attackers who steal service-account credentials or hashes replay them from their own foothold, so a novel source for a high-value identity is an early lateral-movement signal. The rule uses a New Terms detection on the (TargetUserName, source.ip) pair, scoped to accounts matching NBI's service/privileged naming patterns. Maps to ATT&CK Lateral Movement T1078.002 (Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts).
note:
### Investigation
1. Confirm the account is genuinely privileged/service and identify its normal source hosts from prior 4624 history.
2. Pivot on source.ip — a known admin jump host, PAM node, or patch server, or an unrecognized/user-subnet address?
3. Correlate host.name for follow-on 5140/5145 share access or 4672 special privileges, and any type-3 fan-out from the same source.
4. Check for preceding 4776/NTLM or 4769 activity for this account suggesting credential theft or replay.
5. Escalate if the source is unrecognized AND the account touches a sensitive asset (resolve host via known_infrastructure, not a name guess).

### False positives / benign
A service account brought online on a new application, patch, or migration host legitimately produces a novel (account, source.ip) pair. Distinguish by whether the new source is an inventoried server in a change window and whether the account keeps authenticating from it (sustained, single-purpose) versus a one-off logon from a workstation/user subnet followed by fan-out. The 30-day New Terms window suppresses recurring sources but new infrastructure still fires, so correlate to change tickets rather than allowlisting the IP.
author: raadabujaish
query: event.code:"4624" and (winlog.event_data.LogonType:"3" or winlog.event_data.LogonType:"10") and source.ip:* and not source.ip:"::1" and winlog.event_data.TargetUserName:(*Srv or *.admin or *sys_user or ICBS* or SIGCAP* or Sigcap* or *.servacc or *.prod or Docsafe or CITRIX* or Forti* or custody* or Solarwinds* or Veeam* or SCCM* or SP.admin)
